name: Logging and Security Monitoring Policy
description: Defines which components must produce security-relevant logs, where those logs go, how long they are kept, how they are protected, and how alerts arising from them are analysed.
purpose: Establish the coverage, retention, and analysis commitments that the monitoring control is measured against, since none of them are prescribed externally.
scope_guidance: Should cover identity, infrastructure, application, and endpoint log sources within the system boundary, and state the retention period explicitly.

required_elements.element: Log sources required by component type, referenced to the authoritative asset inventory
required_elements.rationale: Coverage cannot be assessed against an undefined source list, and the inventory is the only honest denominator.

required_elements.element: Retention period, stated as at least the examination period
required_elements.rationale: Retention shorter than the period leaves an interval that cannot be evidenced whatever was collected.
Determines whether an attacker with system access could alter the record of their own activity.

required_elements.element: Named responder and analysis timeframe by alert severity
required_elements.rationale: This becomes the commitment against which analysis timeliness is assessed.

required_elements.element: Requirement to record a disposition and its basis for every alert
required_elements.rationale: Distinguishes informed suppression from alerts nobody examined.

required_elements.element: Criteria distinguishing an anomaly from a security event
required_elements.rationale: Defines the handoff into incident evaluation; without it the boundary is improvised.

required_elements.element: Access restrictions on the log store
required_elements.rationale: Log data is frequently more sensitive than the systems producing it.

required_elements.element: Named policy owner, approval record, and review cadence
required_elements.rationale: An unapproved or undated policy is treated as a documentation deficiency.

approval_expectation.approver_role: Executive accountable for security (CISO or equivalent)

communication_expectation: Communicated to engineering teams who own log-producing components and to whoever staffs alert response.
common_gaps: Retention set to a platform default shorter than the examination period.
Source coverage stated generically rather than against the asset inventory.
Analysis timeframe defined with no named responder, so nobody owns it.
No stated criteria for when an anomaly becomes a security event.

source_refs.supports: The criteria the controls this policy documents contribute to.
The required_elements model. SOC 2 prescribes no policy contents.

notes: SOC 2 prescribes no retention period, log source list, or detection rule set. 'expected' means DriftGuard expects the element in a policy intended to support these controls.
